From 25369b22223d1c56e42a0cd4ac9137349d5a898e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 12:32:19 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: rt2x00usb: fix devres lifetime

USB drivers bind to USB interfaces and any device managed resources
should have their lifetime tied to the interface rather than parent USB
device. This avoids issues like memory leaks when drivers are unbound
without their devices being physically disconnected (e.g. on probe
deferral or configuration changes).

Fix the USB anchor lifetime so that it is released on driver unbind.

Fixes: 8b4c0009313f ("rt2x00usb: Use usb anchor to manage URB")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org	# 4.7
Cc: Vishal Thanki <vishalthanki@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Johan Hovold <johan@kernel.org>
Acked-by: Stanislaw Gruszka <stf_xl@wp.pl>
Reviewed-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260327113219.1313748-1-johan@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/ralink/rt2x00/rt2x00usb.c b/drivers/net/wireless/ralink/rt2x00/rt2x00usb.c
index 54599cad78f9..aa5ecade2a40 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/ralink/rt2x00/rt2x00usb.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/ralink/rt2x00/rt2x00usb.c
@@ -828,7 +828,7 @@ int rt2x00usb_probe(struct usb_interface *usb_intf,
 	if (retval)
 		goto exit_free_device;
 
-	rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev,
+	rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev,
 					sizeof(struct usb_anchor),
 					GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!rt2x00dev->anchor) {
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `drivers/net/wireless/ralink/rt2x00/rt2x00usb.c`, to fix the lifetime of the USB anchor resource allocated with `devm_kmalloc`. Specifically:

- **Modification**: In `rt2x00usb_probe`, the allocation's device argument was changed from `&usb_dev->dev` (parent USB device) to `&usb_intf->dev` (USB interface). This ensures that the memory for the USB anchor is tied to the interface's lifetime rather than the parent device's.

- **Relationship**: This change corrects the resource management so that when a USB driver is unbound from the interface (e.g., due to probe deferral, configuration changes, or manual unbind), the anchor is automatically freed. Previously, the anchor would persist until the parent USB device was removed, leading to potential memory leaks and incorrect lifetime semantics. The fix aligns with proper USB driver resource management practices.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev,
					sizeof(struct usb_anchor),
					GFP_KERNEL);
Reason: Using `&usb_dev->dev` ties the resource lifetime to the parent USB device instead of the USB interface (`&usb_intf->dev`). When the driver unbinds from the interface (e.g., on probe deferral or configuration changes), the anchor is not freed because the parent device's lifetime is longer, leading to memory leaks and improper resource cleanup.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
rt2x00dev->anchor = devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev,
					sizeof(struct usb_anchor),
					GFP_KERNEL);
Reason: Using `&usb_intf->dev` ensures that the anchor's lifetime is tied to the USB interface. When the driver unbinds from the interface, the devm resources are automatically freed, preventing memory leaks and ensuring proper cleanup.
